CLAIMS What is claimed is:
1. A method for performing surgery using a robotic system comprising the steps of: providing a tracking system comprising: an instrument configured to be received within a targeted anatomical structure, the instrument including a tracking array, the instrument being a non-cutting tool; a cutting tool configured to remove at least a portion of the targeted anatomical tissue; at least one camera configured to detect a relative position of the instrument within the targeted anatomical structure via the tracking array; and a computer system and a display, the computer system configured to record the relative position of the instrument within the targeted anatomical structure as the instrument is traversed in the targeted anatomical structure, and to illustrate in the display a path of the traversed instrument within the targeted anatomical structure relative to an initial representation of the targeted anatomical structure based on tracking by the camera of the traversed instrument tracking array in the targeted anatomical structure. providing a robot arm coupled to an end effector configured to operatively connected to the instrument, using the robot arm to perform a surgical procedure.
2. The method of claim 1, wherein the computer system is configured to provide an indication based on the relative position of the instrument within the targeted anatomical structure when the instrument encounters a boundary defined by the initial representation of the targeted anatomical structure.
3. The method of claim 1, wherein the computer system is configured to provide a dynamic indicator of an extent of matter remaining in the targeted anatomical structure while the cutting tool removes matter from the targeted anatomical structure.
4. The method of claim 1, wherein a terminal end of the instrument includes an articulable joint, and the instrument includes a secondary tracking marker configured to move relative to the tracking array based on an angle of the articulable joint.
5. The method of claim 4, wherein the articulable joint of the instrument is configured to be selectively actuated to pivot a tip of the instrument within the targeted anatomical structure, and the at least one camera detects a relative position of the tip of the instrument within the targeted anatomical structure via the secondary tracking marker.
6. The method of claim 5, wherein the computer system is configured to compare the position of the tip of the instrument relative to the targeted anatomical structure to the initial representation of the targeted anatomical structure to determine an extent of matter remaining in the targeted anatomical structure.
7. The method of claim 5, wherein the tip of the instrument is adapted to pivot from 0° to 180°.
8. The method of claim 5, wherein the instrument includes a trigger and the articulable joint is actuated by the trigger.
9. The method of claim 1, wherein the end-effector includes a guide tube configured to receive the instrument.
10. The method of claim 1, wherein the robotic arm includes a secondary tracking array, and the at least one camera detects a relative position of the robotic arm to the targeted anatomical structure via the secondary tracking array.
11. The method of claim 1, wherein the robotic arm navigates the instrument within the targeted anatomical structure by comparing data regarding the path of the instrument within the targeted anatomical structure and data regarding the initial representation of the targeted anatomical structure.
12. A method for determining an extent of matter removed from a targeted anatomical structure using a robotic system, comprising the steps of: providing the robotic system with: an instrument configured to be received within a targeted anatomical structure, the instrument including a tracking array; detecting a relative position of the instrument within the targeted anatomical structure via the tracking array and at least one camera; and recording the relative position of the instrument within the targeted anatomical structure, and illustrate in the display a path of the instrument within the targeted anatomical structure relative to an initial representation of the targeted anatomical structure using a computer system and a display,
wherein the targeted anatomical structure is an intervertebral disc disposed in an intervertebral space between adjacent vertebral bodies; removing matter from the targeted anatomical structure using a cutting tool; wherein the instrument other than the cutting tool is configured to be navigated after removing the matter with the cutting tool, within the targeted anatomical structure, wherein the instrument is a non-cutting probing tool; and wherein a position of a tip and shaft of the instrument within the targeted anatomical structure is determined via the tracking array by the computer system.
13. The method of claim 12, wherein the tip of the instrument is enlarged relative to a shaft of the instrument.
14. The method of claim 12, wherein the computer system is configured to determine a position of the shaft of the instrument via the tracking array for tracking the relative position of the instrument within the targeted anatomical structure.
15. The method of claim 12, wherein the computer system is configured to determine a position of the tip of the instrument for tracking the relative position of the instrument within the targeted anatomical structure.
16. The method of claim 12, wherein the computer system is configured to determine a position of the tip of the instrument and the shaft of the instrument for tracking the relative position of the instrument within the targeted anatomical structure.
17. The method of claim 12, wherein a terminal end of the instrument includes an articulable joint, and the instrument includes a secondary tracking marker configured to move relative to the tracking array based on actuation of the articulable joint, wherein the computer system is configured to compare a position of the tip of the instrument within the targeted anatomical structure to the initial representation of the targeted anatomical structure to determine the extent of matter remaining in the targeted anatomical structure.
18. The method of claim 12, wherein the instrument is a probing tool having a ball tip.
19. The method of claim 12, further comprising navigating the instrument along an outer edge of the targeted anatomical structure.
20. The method of claim 18, wherein the ball tip includes a spherical profile.
